title: Negative numbers
summary: What lives to the left of zero, and why −5 is less than −2.

steps.text: Can something be $less$ than nothing? On a winter thermometer, yes: $-3$ degrees is colder than $0$. 👀

steps.caption: To the right of $0$, the usual numbers. To the left, the negatives.

feedback.correct: There it is! $-3$ is three steps to the left of zero.
feedback.incorrect: Negatives live to the left of $0$. Count three steps that way.

hints: Which side of $0$ do negatives live on?

steps.text: On the line, further to the left means $smaller$. That's why $-5$ is below $-2$: the colder it gets, the smaller the number.

feedback.correct: That's it! $-5$ is furthest to the left, so it's the smallest.
feedback.incorrect: Careful: with negatives, the one that looks 'bigger' is actually smaller. Which is furthest left?

hints: Don't trust the size of the digits, look at the position.
The smallest is the one furthest left on the line.

steps.prompt: If you start at $1$ and take $3$ steps to the left, what number do you land on?

feedback.correct: Perfect! $1 \to 0 \to -1 \to -2$. You crossed zero without fear.
feedback.incorrect: Count down one at a time to the left from $1$, and don't stop at $0$.

steps.text: Now you have the whole line, not just half. Negatives are positions, just as real as the positives. 🎉
